articles.title: How to Calculate Profit Margin for an Online Store
articles.excerpt: Originally published on Tool & Till. Revenue is the number most store dashboards put first, but it tells you little about whether the business is working. Two stores with the same sales can end the mo…
articles.body: Originally published on Tool & Till . Revenue is the number most store dashboards put first, but it tells you little about whether the business is working. Two stores with the same sales can end the month in very different places once product costs, shipping, payment fees and ad spend come out. Profit margin is the figure that shows what you actually keep. This guide explains the three margins worth tracking for an online store, which costs belong in each, and where the main store platforms record the data. It uses simple, hypothetical numbers to show the maths; it is not financial or tax advice. The basic formula Profit margin is profit expressed as a share of the selling price: Margin % = (Revenue − Costs) ÷ Revenue × 100 Shopify's own profit reports use the same shape.

articles.title: Memory palace technique: how it works, what studies show
articles.excerpt: Originally published on Mindima Learn. In short: The memory palace technique links each thing you want to remember to a spot along a route you know well, then recalls it by walking that route in your…
articles.body: Originally published on Mindima Learn . In short: The memory palace technique links each thing you want to remember to a spot along a route you know well, then recalls it by walking that route in your mind [3]. In trials it helps most with lists that must be recalled in order, and the biggest gains came after weeks of practice [1, 2]. What is the memory palace technique? The memory palace technique, also called the method of loci, is a way of remembering a list by tying each item to a place you already know well. You picture a familiar building or route, pick a series of spots along it, and leave a vivid image of each item at one spot. To recall the list, you walk the route again in your mind and look at what you left at each stop [3]. The idea is old.

articles.title: 7 Node.js Chunk Boundary Patterns: Retrieval Architecture for Game Listings
articles.excerpt: Short answer: for a retrieval architecture serving a travel itinerary planner or a game-listing index, make each chunk a stable fact, keep volatile fields separate, and carry one listing ID through ev…
articles.body: Short answer: for a retrieval architecture serving a travel itinerary planner or a game-listing index, make each chunk a stable fact, keep volatile fields separate, and carry one listing ID through every record. That boundary keeps search useful without turning the index into a second database. A listing is already a useful unit: title, platform, region, price, release window, and a short description. Split on that boundary before reaching for a character limit. The retriever can then return a complete candidate instead of a paragraph that lost its platform or region. I treat the source payload as an envelope and derive searchable chunks from it. The envelope keeps provenance, while the chunk carries only fields that should participate in semantic matching.

articles.title: yolowpdf 0.2.0: Rebuilding the Math That PDF Throws Away
articles.excerpt: yolowpdf is a pure-Rust PDF-to-Markdown library that parses the format itself — no Poppler, no MuPDF. Version 0.2.0, released this week, is a consolidated release with two halves: the PDF core learned…
articles.body: yolowpdf is a pure-Rust PDF-to-Markdown library that parses the format itself — no Poppler, no MuPDF. Version 0.2.0, released this week, is a consolidated release with two halves: the PDF core learned to reconstruct two-dimensional mathematics from glyph geometry, and the OCR side open-sourced its model suite. This post covers both, with the measured numbers. The problem: text survives PDF extraction, math does not A PDF does not store formulas. It stores glyphs at coordinates: a numerator here, a drawn line under it, a denominator below. A text extractor reading in stream order produces linear soup — the fraction loses which part was on top, a matrix flattens into a column of numbers, the limits of a summation detach and wander into the prose.

articles.title: Converting iPhone Videos to Telegram Video Avatars with ffmpeg
articles.excerpt: I kept sending videos from my iPhone to a Telegram bot and getting nothing usable back. No error message, no avatar, just a silent failure. The clip was a normal 4-second recording, so I spent an even…
articles.body: I kept sending videos from my iPhone to a Telegram bot and getting nothing usable back. No error message, no avatar, just a silent failure. The clip was a normal 4-second recording, so I spent an evening figuring out why. The answer was codec and container. iPhones record HEVC (H.265) inside a .MOV wrapper by default. Telegram's video avatar pipeline expects H.264 in MP4, and HEVC uploads looked fine in the client but never got applied. What the video avatar spec asks for These are the limits I target, based on my own testing: Codec: H.264 (AVC) with yuv420p pixel format Resolution: 800x800, square Duration: 10 seconds or less File size: 2 MB or less Audio: none, strip it Each of these is a separate way to get rejected, and the failure doesn't tell you which one tripped.

articles.excerpt: Your guide to December's full Cold Moon, from peak times to skywatching highlights.
articles.body: The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
articles.excerpt: Explore Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' Monuments in marble, Ejecta prints, Launch Sequence sculptures and interactive Crowded Sky at Heft Gallery in New York City.
articles.body: When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos.

articles.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
articles.excerpt: The FCC has given SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit, a move that could transform the landscape of the final frontier.
articles.body: Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions.
